country.comment: Case study of Amathole District Municipality in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title, Abstract, and Section 1; PDF p. 2, Section 4; PDF p. 6, Acknowledgments

effect_estimate.comment: Qualitative thematic findings accompanied only by descriptive interview percentages and municipal administrative/budget benchmarks quoted by officials; no statistical effect estimate is computed.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Across interviews and focus groups in Amathole District Municipality, non-enforcement of municipal by-laws against illegal connections, >1-year non-implementation of the Rural Household Connection Policy created to legalize illegal connections, political interference and lack of political will, staffing imbalances and skills deficits (reported by 50% and 30% of interviewed officials, respectively), weak municipal financial capacity (reported by 65% of officials; billing collection rate of 27% vs. 95% national standard alongside uncompleted indigent status registrations for Free Basic Water Services; O&M budget at 2% vs. 8% national standard; 80% of Equitable Share grant spent on salaries), financial mismanagement (2019/2020 audit disclaimer), illegal connections/vandalism, drought, and dispersed rural settlement geography resulted in unreliable, unsafe, insufficient, and inequitable rural water access.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF pp. 3-6, Sections 5.1-5.4 and Conclusions

mechanism_certainty.comment: Design ceiling is 2 for a primary qualitative case study appraised with the CASP Qualitative Checklist. Rated 2 because interviews with municipal officials and community focus groups directly document specific legal and administrative mechanisms—inability to enforce municipal by-laws against illegal connections, >1-year non-implementation of the Rural Household Connection Policy, failure of indigent residents to register for Free Basic Water Services resulting in unaffordable billing, shared communal standpipe billing constraints, and stringent conditional grant requirements—shaping rural water access.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines dispersed rural municipal jurisdiction (ELIGIBILITY: service_area), water tariffs/billing, indigent registration requirements, and stringent grant conditions (BURDEN: fees, procedural_steps), indigent exemptions under Free Basic Water Services and the Rural Household Connection Policy to regularize illegal connections (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION: hardship_exception, accommodation), non-enforcement of by-laws against illegal connections/vandalism and lack of consequence management (ENFORCEMENT: sanction), and political interference/lack of political will (political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT, service_area, fees, procedural_steps, hardship_exception, accommodation, sanction, political_coordination

outcome_flags.comment: Examines rural water access, formalization/legalization of illegal household connections under the Rural Household Connection Policy (formal_connection), water supply reliability, quantity, and quality, multi-week outages from unmended taps and cable theft (service_continuity), and inability of indigent rural households to afford water bills (affordability).
outcome_flags.value: formal_connection, water_access, service_reliability, service_quantity, service_quality, affordability, service_continuity

sample_size.comment: Purposive sample in Amathole District Municipality comprising 20 semi-structured interviews (top management officials, councilors, local municipality representatives, satellite heads, academia, and a Water Board representative) and 2 focus group discussions (14 community members total), triangulated with a field tour and municipal/AGSA documents.
sample_size.value: 34 participants in 1 district municipality (20 semi-structured interview participants and 14 community members across 2 focus group discussions), plus participant observation (1 field tour) and secondary document analysis
sample_size.where_found: PDF pp. 2-3, Section 4 (Research Methods); PDF p. 6, Acknowledgments

study_design.comment: Constructivist, inductive primary qualitative case study using purposive sampling and triangulated qualitative methods; despite the 'REVIEW ARTICLE' label in the journal header, Section 4 and Acknowledgments establish primary empirical qualitative data collection.
study_design.value: Qualitative case study (descriptive and explanatory qualitative case study using semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions, participant observation, and secondary document analysis)
